messages:
alex: quick ping — opened PR to tweak the batcher heuristic and KV cache TTL to reduce tail latency variance. tests are green in CI and perf run shows 8% p99 improvement for short requests. would love a quick review and an approval if nothing stands out: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842

maria: assigning a quick look. does this change the prefetch behavior for long sequences (>2k)? worried about extra mem pressure on those traces.

alex: good q — it only reduces the batching cutoff for short-seq paths. long-seq prefetch unchanged. i ran a stress job: `scripts/bench_long_seq.sh --runs 50` and heap stayed stable. snippet from smoke run:```
2026-03-16T09:12:01Z INFO batcher: adjusted_cutoff=48ms
2026-03-16T09:12:02Z INFO kvcache: ttl=30s, entries=120k
```

kevin: i'll take this now, will check kernel/native perf numbers and kv eviction behavior. if all good i can approve in ~30m.

jon: deploy-bot says CI passed but can we do a short canary plan? suggest 10% traffic for 30m, then 50% if no regressions.

alex: +1 on the canary. i'll add a rollout note in PR and schedule the canary after merge. merging window today between 11:00-12:00 PT preferred.

deploy-bot: CI status — all checks passed: 12/12 (unit, integration, perf smoke). :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks, will watch the canary. if kv eviction spikes, ping me immediately. :thumbsup:

kevin: quick nits inline on the PR (naming + one comment on the microbenchmark harness). none are blockers. approving after CI re-run.

alex: thanks all — i'll re-run CI and merge in the 11:00 slot if nothing else pops up. appreciate the quick eyes.
